v.rationale: Both pass their suites (29 and 20 tests). They also behaved the same in every probe: no-Accept requests for a non-numeric ID, another user's order, a forbidden write, a bogus bearer token, a guest POST, a wildcard token, a malformed JSON body and an oversized total all got correct JSON status codes and no class names. Both fixed the default redirect to the missing login route, which would otherwise give no-Accept guests a 500. Both also hide the model class name from the 404 message. impl-2 uses more framework features: a policy with denyAsNotFound, plus a middleware priority change so the ability check runs before binding. That is idiomatic, but it is more ceremony than impl-1's relation-scoped findOrFail, which gets the same result in one line. impl-2 also sets 201 by hand when the framework already does, and it has a latent bug: total_cents is an unsignedInteger with no validation max, so large totals would return a 500 on MySQL. impl-1 is simpler, has no such bug, and has broader tests, including a debug-off 500 test, no-Accept 422/403 tests and a persistence check after validation fails. impl-1 ranks first by a modest margin.
